rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE, so the budget headroom allows a stronger obfuscation push. SUB is nearly free and highly effective on this arithmetic-heavy codec (heavy use of constant tables, index math, and small integer ops), so it stays at maximum security/diversity weight with minimal cost weights. FLA is the primary structural defense for the two hot kernels (adpcm_coder/adpcm_decoder dominate the 700-byte function text), raised to 0.85 security with a moderate runtime-cost weight of 0.4 to keep the dispatch overhead acceptable in the tight per-sample loops. BCF is held at a moderate 0.45-0.5 runtime/size cost since its opaque predicates bloat these already branch-dense functions quickly; combined with FLA it still degrades static analysis meaningfully. IBR complements FLA by breaking the flattened block-to-block edges at low risk. IGV is cheap and adds cross-function diversity, kept active despite only 4 functions since coder/decoder/main share global state (the step-size tables and pointers). SPLIT is effectively disabled: the functions are tiny (38-387 bytes), so splitting adds size and edges without real analysis resistance. ICALL stays low-priority — the program has almost no call sites worth virtualizing, indirect calls add measurable runtime cost in hot loops, and its higher correctness risk isn't worth it on a validated binary.
